clue.text: Comedian's comeback about posh fellows gets laugh

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the comedian word is read from its end back to its start
about means going around, so the turned word wraps itself round the posh-fellows letters

blocks.note: a wag is a joker or wit
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
F is fellow, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A stand-up's witty retort about upper-class gentlemen earns a laugh from the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comedian' suggests a stage comic, but here it is a wit or joker; U for upper-class is a long-standing British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A guffaw is a loud, hearty burst of laughter, so it is a particular kind of laugh.

clue.text: Lightweight stroller's better

definitions.note: read as one who bets, not the comparative adjective

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for gram, a very light weight
an ambler is someone who strolls; the 's joins it to the definition

explanation.surface: A slim walker is judged superior to someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like a comparative, but it is someone who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler is a person who places wagers, which is exactly what a bettor or better does.

clue.text: Female university students approach year positively

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for female
standard abbreviation for university
L is a learner or student, doubled for the plural
standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Women undergraduates face the coming academic year with an upbeat attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Approach' just places the students before the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can mean completely or absolutely, as in being entirely convinced of something.

clue.text: Find out a canister's cracked

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so those letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that a tin container has split open.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain something is to establish or discover it for certain, which is to find it out.

clue.text: Job on island for Pat, perhaps

blocks.note: a post is a position of employment
the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A work placement on an island suits someone called Pat.
explanation.walkthrough: Postman Pat is a British children's TV character who delivers mail in a village; 'perhaps' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Postman Pat is the famous fictional mail carrier, so Pat is an example of this occupation.

clue.text: Indifferent progress with intravenous drug

blocks.note: to pass is to go forward or move on
IV is the medical abbreviation for intravenous
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A patient shows little improvement while on a drip of medication.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone passive accepts things without reacting or taking interest, which is being indifferent.

clue.text: Stick with team

blocks.note: first meaning: a walking pole or rod
second meaning: the employees of an organisation

explanation.surface: Advice to stay loyal to your side.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a long rod carried for support, and the staff of a firm is its body of workers.

clue.text: Drive back by river in carriage having a cocktail

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the word for drive is read backwards
in places the river letter inside the word for carriage

blocks.note: to ram is to drive or force in
carriage here is bearing, the way one walks
standard abbreviation for river
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone reverses a coach beside a river and orders a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' suggests a coach, but here it means posture or way of walking: GAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A margarita is a tequila-based mixed drink served with salt on the rim, so it is a cocktail.

clue.text: Persuaded to shift dung to rear of shed

indicators.note: to shift is to move things about, so the letters of the manure word are rearranged
the rear of a word is its back end, so only the closing letters are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the last two letters of the word

explanation.surface: A gardener is talked into moving manure to the back of the shed.
explanation.definitionFit: To nudge someone is to gently prod or coax them, so nudged means gently persuaded.

clue.text: Search reservists turning up for battle

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means reading from the bottom upwards, so the reservists come backwards

blocks.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Reserve soldiers arriving and searching ahead of a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is fighting between armed forces, so it is used as a synonym for battle.

clue.text: Spiteful false claims about debt

indicators.note: something false is not genuine, so the letters of claims are not in their true order
about means surrounding, so the rearranged claims wrap round the debt

blocks.note: taken as written
an IOU is a written acknowledgment of a debt, 'I owe you'

explanation.surface: Nasty untrue allegations made about money someone owes.
explanation.definitionFit: Malicious behaviour is intended to cause harm, which is what spiteful conduct means.

clue.text: One is taken in by crafty card sharp

indicators.note: a crafty trickster shuffles things, so the letters of card are reworked
being taken in by something means being enclosed within it

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A victim is fooled by a cunning cheat at cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card sharp' reads as one phrase, a cheating gambler, but the wordplay ends at card and sharp is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrid smell or taste is pungent and biting, the same as a sharp one.

clue.text: Cover band?

blocks.note: first meaning: a coating spread over a surface
second meaning: a stratum or stripe within something

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a group that plays other people's songs; the two words are separate meanings of one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer of paint covers a surface, and a layer of rock is a horizontal band or stratum.

clue.text: Short jacket and bag for work

blocks.note: brief means short in duration
a jacket is an outer casing, as on a book or pipe

explanation.surface: An office worker's outfit: a cropped jacket and a work bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short jacket' looks like one garment, but the words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A briefcase is the flat carrying case for papers taken to the office, a bag used for one's job.

clue.text: Kick off again with skill after break

blocks.note: a rest is a pause or break
an art is a skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A football match resumes after half-time, played with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the skill word behind the break word.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart is to begin again, and kicking off is starting a football match.

clue.text: Put brakes on bus for dawdler

blocks.note: to slow is to apply the brakes
a coach is a long-distance bus

explanation.surface: A driver brakes a bus because of someone lingering in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A slowcoach is a British informal word for a person who moves or acts too slowly, a dawdler.

clue.text: Fabulous rampant beast described by quote

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so the quote encloses the beast
a rampant heraldic beast rears up on its hind legs, so the whole construction is reared backwards

blocks.note: to cite is to quote
an ox is a large beast

explanation.surface: A rearing heraldic animal is pictured in a quotation, as if from a fable.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry a rampant beast stands up on its hind legs, so the setter uses it for turning the whole piece back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotic things are strikingly unusual and wonderful, which is one sense of fabulous.

clue.text: Runner regains form to chase gold

indicators.note: to form is to shape, so the letters of regains take a new shape

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry
taken as written

explanation.surface: An athlete gets back into shape to pursue a gold medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chase' puts the anagram after the gold; 'Runner' looks like an athlete but means someone who runs an event.
explanation.definitionFit: An organiser runs or manages an event, so is a runner in that sense.

clue.text: Woman's hat made from good French material

blocks.note: bon is French for good
net is a mesh fabric

explanation.surface: A lady's hat is fashioned from fine French fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonnet is a brimmed head covering tied under the chin, traditionally worn by women and girls.

clue.text: Duo endlessly confuse with silly talk

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of the word for a pair is dropped

blocks.note: a duo is two
to addle is to muddle or confuse

explanation.surface: A pair keep baffling everyone with nonsense chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is trivial or foolish speech or writing, i.e. nonsense.

clue.text: Cobblers' first half own goal was hard

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
OG is the standard abbreviation for own goal
taken as written
H is hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A football report: Northampton Town, nicknamed the Cobblers, conceded a tough own goal in the first half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers' is British slang for nonsense. 'First half' looks like a period of play but gives only the first letter of half.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogwash and cobblers are both informal words for rubbish or nonsense talk.

clue.text: Noted hospital's energies died when I left

indicators.note: when the I has gone away, that single letter is removed from the word for died

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for hospital
E is energy, doubled for the plural
taken as written

explanation.surface: A record noting that a hospital patient's strength failed and they passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed something is to take notice of it, so heeded means paid attention to or noted.

clue.text: Dad wearing cap follows man to landing site

indicators.note: the word for dad wears the cap around it, so sits inside it
follows puts the dad-and-cap piece after the word for man

blocks.note: he is the male pronoun
a lid is a cap or cover
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Father in a hat trails another man towards where the aircraft comes down.
explanation.definitionFit: A helipad is a small marked area where helicopters land and take off.

clue.text: Furious when sailor's idle

blocks.note: AB is an able seaman
to laze is to be idle

explanation.surface: Someone is enraged to find a seaman lounging about.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablaze literally means burning, and figuratively describes someone blazing with anger.

clue.text: Tea bags and cake regularly put out in the wings

indicators.note: things routinely put out of place are displaced, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: T is short for tea, as in tea-time abbreviations
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Refreshments are set out at regular intervals for the performers waiting offstage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' tempts a solver to take alternate letters, but here it belongs with 'put out' as part of the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The wings are the hidden sides of a stage, so being in the wings means being backstage.

clue.text: Set off home with beer mug

indicators.note: something gone off is spoiled or disordered, so the letters of set are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Someone heads home carrying a tankard of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stein is a large earthenware German drinking vessel, typically used for beer.

clue.text: Virtue's foremost in Christmas story

indicators.note: the foremost letter of a word is the one at its front
in places that letter inside the festive word

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
Noel is another name for Christmas

explanation.surface: A seasonal tale whose moral is that goodness comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel is a long fictional prose narrative, which is a kind of story.

clue.text: Spirit is very aged finally in conditioned oak

indicators.note: finally asks for only the closing letter of the word before it
conditioned means treated or altered, so the letters of oak are reworked
in places the selected letter inside the rearranged wood

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for very
the closing letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spirit matured for a long time in seasoned oak barrels.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests whisky in casks; the answer is an unaged spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Vodka is a clear distilled alcoholic drink, and spirit is the general word for such strong liquor.

clue.text: Moderate a beta version

indicators.note: a version is an altered form, so the letters appear in a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Software talk: tone down a test release.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate is to lessen or reduce in intensity, which is to moderate as a verb.

clue.text: Smart kitchen furniture not finished ahead of party

blocks.note: a dresser is a kitchen cupboard with open shelves above
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: An elegant kitchen cabinet is left incomplete before a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dressed up is wearing their best formal clothes, so looks smart.

clue.text: Raise for worker briefly entering enclosure close to crocodile

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the worker word goes
entering means going inside, so the shortened worker goes into the enclosure
the close of a word is its end, so only the last letter of crocodile is kept

blocks.note: enc. is the abbreviation for enclosure at the foot of a letter
a hand is a manual worker
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A zoo worker gets a pay rise for going into the crocodile pen.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance is to improve or increase something, which is one sense of raise.

clue.text: Banks in Ecuador take currency commission

indicators.note: banks are the edges of a river, so only the outer letters of the country are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: Banks in South America charge a fee for exchanging money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' and 'currency' suggest finance, and 'commission' a fee; here commission means a task.
explanation.definitionFit: A commission is a task someone is given to carry out, and an errand is a small such job.
